newsitem.title: INDIA: India's rulers postpone oil price decision again.
newsitem.headline: India's rulers postpone oil price decision again.

text.p: India's ruling United Front coalition, divided over how to control a mounting oil subsidy bill, postponed a decision on Monday on whether to raise petroleum product prices, alliance members said.

Railways Minister Ram Vilas Paswan told reporters after the 2-1/2-hour meeting of the centre-left alliance's Steering Committee that the issue of the mounting oil subsidy bill had been deferred until a meeting on June 27.
It was the second time in three weeks that the 15-party coalition failed to reach a consensus.
Information Minister Jaipal Reddy, who is the United Front's spokesman, said there was some discussion of the issue of oil prices. "But the discussion was inconclusive," he said.

The leftwing parties in Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's coalition have steadfastly opposed raising the prices of some petroleum products such as kerosene and diesel to plug the government's mounting debt to state oil companies.
The government owed domestic oil firms 155 billion rupees ($4.3 billion) at the end of March as compensation for selling some petroleum products below world market levels.
Gujral and Finance Minister P. Chidambaram has said some prices might have to be raised to rein in the cost to the government.

Last July, only weeks after the United Front took power, the government raised the price of gasoline by 25 percent, and prices of high-speed diesel, liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) for cooking, paraffin wax and fuel oil by 30 percent.
But it was forced to scale back the increase in diesel prices to 15 percent after nationwide protests led by the leftwing parties.
The Communist Party of India (Marxist) has submitted an alternative plan to the Steering Committee that seeks to avoid hurting the poor.
The plan calls for the government to return to the state-run oil sector surplus funds taken from it by earlier governments as well as the elimination of customs and excise duties.
United Front leaders have blamed the previous Congress government for not raising the prices of petroleum products in the last 2-1/2 years of Congress rule.
The previous Congress government's only increase was in February 1994, and applied to gasoline and diesel.
